meta.title: WaniKani card suitability review: source levels 2–5
meta.scope: All 403 visible source-level 2–5 Japanese catalog vocabulary entries, including inactive library entries; one retired record retained for completeness.
meta.basis: Catalog meanings/readings, visual concepts, existing semantic review notes, representative artwork, and selected official WaniKani sense checks. This is exercise-suitability advice, not a new full-resolution media or pronunciation approval.
meta.englishMeaningAnswerPolicy: Optional means a sense-specific English meaning exercise is a useful candidate, not that every review should use English. No means no dedicated English-answer recommendation, not a ban on English onboarding or accessibility support. English meaning answers would be a proposed new exercise; existing writing choices use Japanese.
meta.contextPolicy: Context required means avoid a standalone illustration quiz. Contextual questions can still use pictures, quantities, maps or Japanese text as answers. Optional English meaning answers may also be used, with context whenever the isolated audio is ambiguous.

items.recommendation: Establish acquiring a skill or studying a subject in a short account.
items.englishNote: Learn or study can check the intended acquisition/study sense without treating a book icon as sufficient.
items.currentVisualConcept: Learner connects an open book to a new idea bulb.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Reading leads to a new idea as a symbol for learning.

items.rationale: Construction or preparation is visible if the resulting product follows an observable making process.
items.recommendation: Show hands assembling materials into a simple model, with a compact before-and-after sequence; avoid a finished object alone.
items.currentVisualConcept: Hands assemble blocks into a small house.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Constructing a model house represents making.

items.rationale: Two people merely standing together do not depict the event of meeting.
items.recommendation: Use a short convergence-and-greeting sequence with the same characters; context can distinguish a planned meeting from passing by.
items.currentVisualConcept: Two approaching people greet each other in the middle.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: People converging and greeting symbolize meeting.

items.rationale: Mixing can be shown by an actor combining distinct contents rather than a static bowl.
items.recommendation: Use a before-and-after stirring or combining scene; context should later establish which mix spelling/sense is intended.
items.currentVisualConcept: Kiku stirring pink and yellow batter in a bowl with a wooden spoon.

items.rationale: Rotation is directly observable across changing orientations, whereas a still pinwheel may mean the object.
items.recommendation: Use a fixed center and a short rotation sequence; keep circular motion distinct from counting occurrences.
items.currentVisualConcept: Pinwheel rotates around a fixed hub.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Pinwheel and rotation arrows show revolving.

items.rationale: A clear dynamic running pose is a recognizable action.
items.recommendation: Keep bent arms, stride and motion cues readable; use context for vehicles or figurative senses later.
items.currentVisualConcept: Runner leans forward with bent arms and long strides.

items.rationale: A speech bubble alone cannot distinguish saying something from talking, asking or showing a voice.
items.recommendation: Use a brief quoted utterance or a natural reporting sentence with an explicit speaker.
items.englishNote: Say can clarify the intended reporting action without accepting every communication verb.
items.currentVisualConcept: Person speaks a small three-dot bubble toward a listener.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Speech bubble shows saying something.

items.rationale: Setting an object upright is visible if the actor and orientation change are shown.
items.recommendation: Show hands turning the same horizontal object upright; exclude a person simply standing as an equivalent picture.
items.currentVisualConcept: Hands rotate a horizontal board into an upright position.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Transitive action sets a board upright; distinguish from standing up oneself.

items.rationale: Stopping requires a change from movement to stillness and differs from someone actively stopping another object.
items.recommendation: Show an object moving and then halted, with no external agent supplying the stop; use sentence context to teach 止める versus 止まる.
items.currentVisualConcept: Moving ball halts against a firm stop bar.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Motion lines terminate at barrier to symbolize stopping.

items.rationale: Taking something out is visible if an actor moves an object across a container boundary.
items.recommendation: Show a hand lifting a ball out of an open box with a clear rim and before-and-after positions.
items.currentVisualConcept: Ball is lifted out of an open box.

items.rationale: A thought bubble may indicate an idea, worry, remembering or understanding rather than thinking about a stated issue.
items.recommendation: Give the person a concrete choice or problem to consider in a short situation.
items.englishNote: Think about or consider is useful for the selected cognitive action.
items.currentVisualConcept: Person thinks about a puzzle piece inside a thought bubble.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Thought bubble with unfinished puzzle represents thinking.

items.rationale: A light bulb or fitted puzzle is an arbitrary comprehension metaphor and overlaps with learning and thinking.
items.recommendation: Use a situation where an explanation becomes understood or a fact becomes known.
items.englishNote: Understand or know should match the actual construction, avoiding a universal light-bulb answer.
items.currentVisualConcept: Two puzzle pieces fit together under a bright idea spark.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Pieces fitting and idea spark symbolize comprehension.

items.rationale: A train and direction arrow do not establish the destination-bound suffix or the ゆき reading.
items.recommendation: Use a natural destination announcement or route statement, with a departure board as supporting reference.
items.englishNote: Bound for ... is more accurate for the destination suffix than the broad gloss Train Direction.
items.currentVisualConcept: A train traveling right beneath a right-pointing sign reading 東京.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Destination-bound train symbolizes 行き read ゆき; this word also functions as a destination suffix.

items.rationale: Vehicle movement can be observed, whereas a travel scene may incorrectly suggest tourism.
items.recommendation: Show the same vehicle progressing along a road in a short sequence; clarify the gloss as vehicle travel or running rather than travel in general.
items.currentVisualConcept: Vehicle moves along a road with strong motion streaks.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Vehicle motion represents traveling/running of a vehicle, rather than tourism.

items.rationale: A clear triangle directly depicts the shape.
items.recommendation: Use an uncomplicated three-sided outline and avoid confusing rotation or size changes with a different shape.
items.currentVisualConcept: A plain lavender triangle.

items.rationale: An academic-looking building and graduation cap do not uniquely distinguish a university from another school.
items.recommendation: Introduce a university in a study or campus situation; architecture may support the setting rather than prove its institutional type.
items.currentVisualConcept: A university hall with arched entrance and graduation cap.

items.rationale: A timeline ending at a clock needs a current reference and an ongoing proposition.
items.recommendation: State something that has continued up to now; use an anchored timeline only as support.
items.englishNote: Until now or up to now can clarify the temporal span without confusing it with now alone.
items.currentVisualConcept: Timeline of completed steps ends at a highlighted current clock.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Past-to-present span ending at current clock represents until now.

items.rationale: A valley is a distinctive landform between higher slopes.
items.recommendation: Make the low region between slopes dominant; avoid showing only a mountain peak or river.
items.currentVisualConcept: A grassy valley with a winding blue river, lavender rocky mountain slopes and small snowy peaks.

items.rationale: A mixed pile of colored objects may mean color, many or different rather than various kinds.
items.recommendation: Describe a range of kinds or experiences, keeping number and color incidental.
items.englishNote: Various kinds of ... can make the intended variety sense clear.
items.currentVisualConcept: A collection of differently colored shapes and objects.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: A varied collection symbolizes various.

items.rationale: A person with drawn waves might mean speak, say or sound and depends on a symbolic sound convention.
items.recommendation: Use actual human voice in a listening situation and contrast environmental sound through the source of the audio.
items.englishNote: Voice provides a precise semantic contrast with general sound when context identifies the source.
items.currentVisualConcept: Person produces small curved voice waves from mouth.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Human source distinguishes voice from bell sound and larger waves distinguish loud voice.

items.rationale: A consistent north-up compass or map directly encodes west.
items.recommendation: Use a taught compass frame with west highlighted; avoid an unanchored left arrow or a sunset scene alone.
items.currentVisualConcept: Compass highlights the leftward direction with a setting sun.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Map convention uses north up and west left; no direction caption.

items.rationale: A map with a compass and multiple exits can identify the west exit unambiguously.
items.recommendation: Show a simple station plan, fixed north orientation and west-side exit; do not equate west with whichever doorway appears left in a perspective drawing.
items.currentVisualConcept: Building exit on the left with westward compass cue.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Left exit and compass symbolize west exit; orientation requires review.

items.rationale: A question mark represents questioning in general, not specifically asking what.
items.recommendation: Use a natural question about an object or action and provide meaningful object/action answers.
items.currentVisualConcept: A large violet question mark.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Mystery containers symbolize what; inherently abstract.

items.rationale: A calendar question mark is a mnemonic and does not demonstrate comprehension of a month question.
items.recommendation: Ask what month an event happens and answer with an actual month or month reference card.
items.currentVisualConcept: Clean month calendar page with a single large question in place of the month number.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Question in month page represents which month; distinguish from how many days.

items.rationale: A year-like string of question marks cannot decide which-year from how-many-years without a sentence.
items.recommendation: Use an event-year or duration question with the actual year or year count as answers.
items.currentVisualConcept: Clean year calendar page with four unresolved year digits and no day grid.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Four question marks occupy year digits to cue what year.

items.rationale: A cereal grain ear is directly depictable, though the word's scope can be broader than wheat.
items.recommendation: Use a clear grain-ear picture for the taught sense and verify whether the lesson should acknowledge wheat/barley scope; avoid unsupported species contrasts.
items.currentVisualConcept: Three golden ears of wheat on stalks.

items.rationale: A baby-to-elderly sequence is a life-stage mnemonic rather than an assertion spanning someone's whole life.
items.recommendation: Use a lifelong commitment or duration sentence with a life timeline only as support.
items.englishNote: One's whole life or for life can clarify the duration in the chosen construction.
items.currentVisualConcept: Life arc spans baby, adult, and elderly person.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Life stages span a whole life; age depiction is schematic.

items.rationale: An office cutaway depicts physical interior, while the target commonly concerns internal company scope.
items.recommendation: Use internal company communication or rules; distinguish the homophone 車内 using full spoken context.
items.englishNote: Within the company or internal to the company checks the organizational sense rather than merely inside an office.
items.currentVisualConcept: Cutaway office shows people working inside its walls.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Interior office view represents within the company.

items.rationale: A yarn ball and knitting needles directly convey the concrete material.
items.recommendation: Keep the yarn strand and ball prominent; exclude 糸 when the images overlap and use context for material distinctions.
items.currentVisualConcept: A ball of lavender wool yarn with two knitting needles.

items.rationale: A pointing gesture cannot fix you without a speaker, addressee and conversational viewpoint.
items.recommendation: Use a short dialogue with stable named speaker/listener positions and ask who is addressed.
items.currentVisualConcept: Foreground speaker points toward the facing listener.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Directed attention toward the listener symbolizes you; conversational pronouns require review.

items.rationale: A shorter person is not necessarily younger and no appearance proves a sibling relationship.
items.recommendation: Introduce named siblings and ages in a family situation; use a family tree only as support.
items.currentVisualConcept: Younger shorter brother is highlighted beside older sibling.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Relative age and branch cue younger brother; family and gender need review.

items.rationale: An energetic person with a shoulder bag does not establish the intended young-person age category.
items.recommendation: Introduce the person's life stage and age in context; avoid image-only competition with boy or adult man.
items.englishNote: A young person or young adult can clarify the intended sense more accurately than an ambiguous standalone Youth answer.
items.currentVisualConcept: Young adult walks energetically with a shoulder bag.
items.currentVisualReviewNote: Youth age category and gender cannot reliably be read from appearance; review against boy and adult man.
